action.question: How should `fork-all` decide which sessions to fork?

questions.question: How should `fork-all` decide which sessions to fork?

options.label: --host <nick> required
options.description: User must pass `--host mini` or `--host note`. Matches against the session's title prefix (e.g. `[AH.mini]`) AND the worktree-index for that host. No implicit 'this-host' — explicit only.

options.label: --host plus --id list
options.description: `--host mini` filters by host; OR pass `--id cse_xxx --id cse_yyy` to fork an explicit set regardless of host. Lets you cherry-pick when the title prefix is missing.

options.label: --host with --this-host shortcut
options.description: `--host <nick>` is the canonical form; `--this-host` is sugar that resolves to whatever this machine's nickname is (mini/note from $(hostname)).

questions.question: How does fork-all locate the on-disk transcript for an orphaned cse_ session?

options.label: Reuse find_source_jsonl (worktree dirname match)
options.description: Existing logic: glob `~/.claude/projects/*bridge-cse-<tail>` and pick newest .jsonl. Works only if the bridge worktree dir is still present locally.

options.label: Same, but require worktree present
options.description: Reuse find_source_jsonl AND verify the bridge worktree dir still exists under ~/dev. If not present, skip with a warning instead of erroring — covers the case where worktree was removed before fork-all runs.

options.label: Scan all project dirs for sessionId match
options.description: Slower but bulletproof: open every .jsonl under ~/.claude/projects and check if its sessionId equals the cse_ id. Lets fork-all work even if the worktree dir was renamed/removed.

questions.question: Archive flow after a successful fork (your point #3)?

options.label: Per-session: fork → verify → archive, one at a time
options.description: For each cse_: do_fork; if dest .jsonl exists and line_count > 0, then archive_session(cse_id); on any failure, abort archive for that one and keep going. Safest — partial failures don't lose work.

options.label: Two-phase: fork all, then archive all that succeeded
options.description: Phase 1: fork every session, collect (cse_id, success) pairs. Phase 2: archive only the successes. Clearer logs but holds twice the state in memory; no real upside over per-session.

options.label: Fork only; archive is a separate subcommand
options.description: `fork-all` never archives. Add `python3 -m remote_control sessions archive <cse_id>...` separately. Manual two-step, but archival becomes reusable for other workflows (manager executor in #27, etc.).

questions.question: Where does the supervisor automation live?

options.label: Post-spawn hook in Supervisor.tick()
options.description: After the first tick where all wanted servers are confirmed running, run fork-all against the list of cse_ ids that WERE running before this supervisor instance started. Gated by env var. Self-healing on every restart.

options.label: Separate launchd job, RunAtLoad
options.description: A second plist that runs `fork-all --host <this>` once after the supervisor's plist has had time to spawn its servers (sleep + run). Decouples it from the supervisor's tick loop entirely.

options.label: Skip automation; manual fork-all only
options.description: Just ship the CLI. You run it yourself after `launchctl kickstart -k`. Defers the automation decision until the manual flow is proven.

transcript_tail.text:
Looking at what's there: the existing `fork` command already does the right thing per-session (copies the `.jsonl` to a fresh uuid, rewrites cwd `--into-main`, retitles the source with `--mark`), and the supervisor's `shutdown_all()` is the choke point that nukes the `mm-*` servers on every kickstart. So we already have the per-session primitive; what's missing is bulk + automation.

Current state on mini: `python3 -m remote_control sessions` shows 5 `this-host` bridge sessions, of which 3 are already disconnected+forked (the `→ forked to …` titles) and only 2 are live (`Remote control titles apply` idle, `macmini-local-cozy-piglet` running). So a useful "fork-all" is genuinely just a handful per cycle.

### Recommendation

**(1) Right now — a `fork-all` subcommand** that wraps `do_fork` over the result of `session_list`, filtered to `location == this-host` and not already-forked (skip titles ending in `→ forked to …`). Defaults: `--into-main`, `--mark`, no `--run` (resuming is the human's call). Optional `--archive` flag for the originals (needs adding a tiny `archive_session(cse_id)` to `usage_limit/monitor.py` against the existing API client). One command, dry-runnable, idempotent.

**(2) Automation — pre-shutdown hook in `Supervisor.shutdown_all()`**, gated by an env var (`SUPERVISOR_FORK_ON_SHUTDOWN=1`), that calls the same `fork-all` *before* it TERMs the servers. That way every `launchctl kickstart -k` automatically lays down local siblings with full history. Resume is still manual (the supervisor restart re-creates fresh `cse_` sessions per dir — there's no API to make a fresh server adopt an old cse_), but the work is never lost.

**Main tradeoff**: forking ≠ auto-resume. The forks are independently resumable transcripts; the user still has to `claude -r <new_sid>` in the right cwd to continue. Auto-resume would mean spawning headless `claude -r … -p` workers post-restart, which is a much bigger feature and arguably worse than letting the human pick which threads to revive.

Want me to build (1) first as a standalone `python3 -m remote_control fork-all` and verify against your current 2 live sessions, then wire (2) on top? Or pull the trigger on both in one pass?
